extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, and USPTO examiners (practitioners handling patent term adjustment and prosecution timing)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and criteria for calculating patent term adjustment (PTA) and reductions under 35 U.S.C. 154 and implementing regulations (37 CFR 1.702–1.704), including what periods count for adjustment, what applicant actions reduce adjustment, and how to measure overlapping periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable claims remain in the application
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim is considered to 'remain in the application' (and thus affects adjustment) when: (1) at least one claim is allowable at the time the examiner’s answer is mailed and is not canceled before, or made subject to a rejection as a result of, the appellate review; or (2) when all of the rejections applied to at least one claim are reversed, and such claim is not made subject to a rejection as a result of the appellate review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (A) If claim 2 was allowable prior to appeal and not canceled, allowable claims remain. (B) If claim 2 was only objected to (allowable except for dependency), it is not 'allowable' for PTA purposes. (C) If rejection of claim 2 is reversed on appeal and it is not subject to any outstanding objection, it is 'allowable' (see MPEP § 1214.06 II).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board decision counted as a PTAB 'decision' under 35 U.S.C. 134/135
rubrics_metrics.description: For a Board decision to be a 'decision by the Patent Trial and Appeal Board under [35 U.S.C.] 134' (and similar for 135), the decision must sustain or reverse the rejection(s) of the claim(s) on appeal, or in limited circumstances a remand may be deemed a decision. For 135 the decision must include a decision on patentability of claims, derivation, or priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A remand by a panel may be considered a decision for purposes of PTA only if it's the last panel action prior to mailing of a notice of allowance; but not if later a request for continued examination (RCE) is filed without an intervening mailing of an action under 132 or a notice of allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'final decision' for 37 CFR 1.703(a)(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Final decision' means: (1) the decision is the last decision in the review by the Board (or by a federal court); and (2) the decision does not require further action by the applicant to avoid termination of proceedings as to the rejected claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Board decision containing a new ground of rejection under 37 CFR 41.50(b) requires applicant action and is not a 'final decision' for 1.703(a)(5). 'Final decision' for 1.703(a)(5) does not require finality for judicial review (e.g., reversal of all rejections can be 'final' for PTA even if not appeal-final).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(a)(6) measurement for 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(1)(A)(iv)
rubrics_metrics.description: The period is the number of days, if any, beginning on the day after the date that is four months after the date the issue fee was paid and all outstanding requirements were satisfied and ending on the date the patent was issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date the issue fee was paid and all outstanding requirements were satisfied is the later of the issue fee payment date or the date all outstanding requirements were satisfied. Filing a priority document is not an 'outstanding requirement' for this provision. If prosecution reopens after allowance, the date moves to the issue fee transmittal form (PTOL-85(b)) from the ultimate notice of allowance and any remaining requirements must be satisfied before counting.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTA for Office delay in acting on an RCE (37 CFR 1.702(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is provided PTA when the Office fails to act on a request for continued examination (RCE) within four months of the filing of the RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The adjustment period begins the day after the date that is four months from filing the RCE and ends on the date of mailing of an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(b) (three-year period) and statutory exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of adjustment under 1.702(b) is the number of days in the period beginning on the day after three years after the actual filing date of the application and ending on the date a patent was issued; 1.703(b) sets out limitations excluding certain periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluded (not counted toward PTA) are periods for continued examination under 35 U.S.C. 132(b), interference proceedings, periods due to a secrecy order, and appellate review under 134/141/145. Applicant-requested delays are addressed in 1.704 as applicant failures to engage in reasonable efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Circuit interpretation of 'time consumed by continued examination' (Novartis v. Lee)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Circuit held: (1) any time consumed by continued examination under 35 U.S.C. 132(b) is subtracted in determining how much the three-year period is exceeded regardless of when the continued examination was initiated; (2) the time consumed does not include time after a notice of allowance is mailed unless the Office actually resumes examination of the application after allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This case law affects how continued examination time is treated when measuring the three-year period under 154(b)(1)(B)(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2015 amendment to measurement of time consumed by RCE (37 CFR 1.703(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective Jan 9, 2015, the time consumed by continued examination under 35 U.S.C. 132(b) is the number of days in the period beginning on the date any request for continued examination was filed and ending on the date of mailing of the notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change applies to any patent granted before, on, or after Jan 9, 2015. Time between an RCE and a notice of allowance counts even if the Office issued no Office action under 132. Periods may be non-contiguous if multiple RCEs are filed after notices of allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation rules for multiple RCEs and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple RCEs are filed and notices of allowance occur before/after them, the 'time consumed by continued examination' may include non-contiguous periods: count from each RCE filing date to the mailing date of the notice of allowance following that RCE; if multiple consecutive notices of allowance/PTOL-85s occur, measure to the first PTOL-85.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a first RCE is filed before a notice of allowance and a second is filed after a notice of allowance, count both RCE-to-allowance periods. If multiple RCEs occur without an intervening allowance, count from the first RCE filing to the notice of allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(c) adjustment for interference/derivation
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of adjustment under 1.702(c) is the sum of: (1) days from institution of an interference or derivation involving the application to termination of that proceeding with respect to the application; and (2) days from suspension of prosecution due to interference/derivation proceedings under 35 U.S.C. 135(a) not involving the application to termination of the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periods are summed to extent they do not overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(d) adjustment for secrecy orders/sealed condition
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of adjustment under 1.702(d) is the sum of: (1) days the application was maintained in sealed condition under 35 U.S.C. 181; (2) days from mailing of an examiner's answer under 37 CFR 41.39 while under secrecy to removal of the secrecy order; (3) days from notification that an interference/derivation would be instituted but for the secrecy order to removal of secrecy order; (4) days from notification under 37 CFR 5.3(c) to mailing of notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151 and 37 CFR 1.311.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periods are summed to the extent not overlapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(e) adjustment when jurisdiction passes to PTAB
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of adjustment under 1.702(e) is the number of days from the date jurisdiction over the application passes to the PTAB under 37 CFR 41.35(a) (or 41.31 for earlier allowances) to the date of a final decision in favor of the applicant by the Board or by a federal court on appeal under 35 U.S.C. 141 or a civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts only when the final decision is in favor of the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(f) overlapping periods and cap on adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustment runs from the expiration date of the patent and, to the extent periods under 1.703(a)–(e) overlap, the period of adjustment will not exceed the actual number of days the issuance of the patent was delayed (35 U.S.C. 154(b)(2)(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wyeth v. Kappos clarified that periods overlap under 154(b)(2)(A) only if the periods occur on the same calendar day. The date on a certificate of mailing/transmission under 37 CFR 1.8 is not used in PTA calculation (only for timeliness); actual date of receipt in the Office (PALM) is used for calculation. Applicants should use EFS, Priority Mail Express to get earliest filing date; PAIR/PALM dates determine final PTA calculation; reductions reinstated require fee and showing.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(g) disclaimer limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: No patent whose term has been disclaimed beyond a specified date shall be adjusted under 37 CFR 1.702 and 1.703 beyond the expiration date specified in the disclaimer (35 U.S.C. 154(b)(2)(B)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A PTA cannot extend a patent beyond a voluntary terminal disclaimer date.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(a) general reduction rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of adjustment of the term of a patent under § 1.703(a) through (e) shall be reduced by a period equal to the period of time during which the applicant failed to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution (processing or examination) of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1.704 implements 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(2)(C) and authorizes regulations establishing circumstances that constitute failure to engage in reasonable efforts. The reduction applies regardless of whether the applicant's action/inaction caused or contributed to PTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(b) three-month reply rule (deemed failure)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant shall be deemed to have failed to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination for the cumulative total of any periods of time in excess of three months taken to reply to any notice or action by the Office making any rejection, objection, argument, or other request, measuring the three-month period from the date the notice or action was mailed or given to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the cumulative excess exceeds three months, the period of adjustment is reduced by days beginning the day after the date that is three months after mailing/transmission of the Office communication and ending on the date the reply was filed. The Office action's shortened statutory reply period has no effect on this three-month measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(1) suspension of action under § 1.103
rubrics_metrics.description: If prosecution is suspended under § 1.103 at the applicant’s request, the PTA period is reduced by the number of days from the date a request for suspension was filed to the date of termination of the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts only to the extent not overlapping with other reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(2) deferral of issuance under § 1.314
rubrics_metrics.description: If issuance is deferred under § 1.314 at the applicant’s request, reduce PTA by days from the date a request for deferral was filed to the date the patent was issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduction limited to the duration of the deferral (non-overlapping).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(3) abandonment or late payment of issue fee
rubrics_metrics.description: For abandonment or late issue fee payment, reduce PTA by days beginning on the date of abandonment or the date after the issue fee was due and ending on the earlier of: (i) mailing of the decision reviving the application or accepting late issue fee payment; or (ii) four months after filing a grantable petition to revive or accept late payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires counting from abandonment/late payment to revival or the four-month cap when a petition is grantable.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(4) failure to file petition to withdraw abandonment holding
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant fails to file a petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment or to revive within two months from the mailing date of a notice of abandonment, reduce PTA by days beginning the day after two months from the mailing date and ending on the date such petition was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure from two months after notice of abandonment to filing of the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(5) conversion of provisional to nonprovisional
rubrics_metrics.description: When converting a provisional application under 35 U.S.C. 111(b) to a nonprovisional under 111(a), reduce PTA by days beginning on the date the application was filed under 111(b) and ending on the date a compliant § 1.53(c)(3) request to convert was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to conversion delays attributable to applicant for PTA reduction purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(6) preliminary amendment or paper filed <1 month before action
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a preliminary amendment or other preliminary paper less than one month before mailing of an Office action or notice of allowance that requires a supplemental Office action or notice of allowance causes PTA reduction equal to the lesser of: (i) days from day after original mailing to supplementary mailing; or (ii) four months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This penalizes late preliminary papers that necessitate extra Office work; cap is four months.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(7) reply having an omission (§ 1.135(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reply containing an omission is filed, reduce PTA by days from the day after the filing date of the reply with omission to the date the omission-correcting reply or paper was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses delays caused by deficiencies in applicant replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(8) unsolicited supplemental reply/paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a supplemental reply or other paper (not expressly requested by the examiner) after a reply has been filed reduces PTA by days from the day after the initial reply filing to the date the supplemental paper was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourages filing additional materials that prolong prosecution unless requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(9) amendment after Board/court decision <1 month before action
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of an amendment or paper after a Board decision (not a new-ground decision) or Federal court decision less than one month before mailing of an Office action or notice of allowance that requires a supplemental mailing reduces PTA by the lesser of: (i) days from the day after original mailing to supplemental mailing; or (ii) four months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar late-submission penalty as (6) but following post-decision amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(10) amendment or paper after notice of allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of an amendment under § 1.312 or other paper (except an RCE under § 1.114) after a notice of allowance has been given or mailed reduces PTA by the lesser of: (i) days from filing of the amendment/paper to the mailing date of the Office action or notice responding; or (ii) four months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-allowance amendments that trigger further Office action reduce PTA, capped at four months.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(11) failure to file appeal brief in compliance with § 41.37 within three months
rubrics_metrics.description: If an appeal brief is not filed in compliance with § 41.37 within three months from the date a notice of appeal was filed under 35 U.S.C. 134 and § 41.31, reduce PTA by days beginning on the day after three months from the notice of appeal filing and ending on the date a compliant appeal brief or a RCE under § 1.114 is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured from three months after notice of appeal to filing of compliant brief or RCE; non-compliance causes PTA reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(12) filing an RCE after a notice of allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing an RCE under 35 U.S.C. 132(b) after any notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151 was mailed reduces PTA by days beginning the day after the mailing date of the notice of allowance and ending on the date the RCE was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCEs filed post-allowance count as applicant delays reducing PTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(13) failure to provide application in condition for examination within eight months
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to provide an application in condition for examination as defined in paragraph (f) within eight months from filing under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) or from commencement of the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371 for international applications reduces PTA by days beginning the day after that eight-month date and ending on the date the application is in condition for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines an applicant-caused delay when required papers are not timely provided; see paragraph (f) for 'in condition for examination' elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(14) further prosecution via a continuing application
rubrics_metrics.description: When prosecution continues via a continuing application, the PTA for the resulting patent shall not include any period that is prior to the actual filing date of the application that resulted in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periods before the actual filing date of the eventual patent application are excluded from PTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(d) IDS-only filing exception
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper containing only an information disclosure statement (IDS) complying with §§ 1.97 and 1.98, or an RCE with only an IDS, will not be considered a failure under certain paragraphs if accompanied by a statement that each item was first cited in a communication from a patent office (counterpart foreign/international or Office) not received by a designated individual more than 30 days prior to filing, or is a communication issued by a patent office not received by a designated individual more than 30 days prior to filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 30-day period is not extendable. This protects applicants filing IDSs prompted by recent office communications from being penalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(e) reinstatement request not treated as failure
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a request under § 1.705(c) for reinstatement of reduced patent term adjustment will not be considered a failure to engage in reasonable efforts under paragraph (c)(10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a reinstatement request to undo a previously reduced PTA (pursuant to § 1.705(c)) does not itself create further applicant-failure reductions under (c)(10).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(f) 'in condition for examination' definition
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) is 'in condition for examination' when it includes: a specification including at least one claim and an abstract (§ 1.72(b)); papers in compliance with § 1.52; drawings if any in compliance with § 1.84; any required English translations (§ 1.52(d)/1.57(a)); a sequence listing where applicable (§§ 1.821–1.825); the inventor's oath/declaration or an ADS (§ 1.63(b)); basic filing fee, search fee, examination fee; any certified copy required by § 1.57(a); and any application size fee required under § 1.16(s). International national-stage applications have analogous requirements (§ 1.492 fees etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application is considered to have papers/drawings/sequence listing in compliance for purposes of this paragraph on the filing date of the latest prior reply correcting those items if that reply is prior to mailing of an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance, whichever occurs first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory authority and policy rationale for 1.704
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.704 implements 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(2)(C) by specifying circumstances constituting a failure of an applicant to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing/examination and that PTA shall be reduced by the period of such failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute authorizes the Office to prescribe regulations establishing circumstances that constitute failure; reductions apply regardless of whether applicant's actions caused or contributed to PTA. The provisions aim to balance PTA for Office delays with public interest in timely availability of patented technology.
